chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Hamdan al-Qalanisi, from Is'haq ibn Bunan, from Ibn Baqqah, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), when the one who took the solemn oath refused to divorce, would make an enclosure for him from cane and give him a quarter of his provision until he divorces.

key_terms.الْمُؤْلِي: The one who takes the oath of abstention from intimacy
key_terms.رُبُعَ قُوتِهِ: A quarter of his food provision

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali enforce divorce when a husband refused to end his oath of abstention?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the practical application of *al-iman* (oath of abstention) by Imam Ali (peace be upon him), employing a coercive measure of physical isolation and dietary restriction to compel the husband to divorce. It highlights the juristic principle that the oath-taker's refusal to fulfill the conditional divorce triggers a punitive enforcement mechanism, reflecting the early Shia emphasis on resolving marital disputes through authoritative judicial intervention.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Hamdan Al Qalanasy, from Is’haq Bin Bunan, from Ibn Baqqah, from Giyas Bin Ibrahim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>, when the solemn oather refused to divorce, he<sup>asws</sup> made an enclosure from cane, and gave him a quarter of his provision until he divorces’.
en.sarwar: 12. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtariy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

If a man angers his wife and does not go to bed with her without swearing for four months and she complains against him, he then must expiate or divorce her. If he leaves her without anger or swearing, then the rules of 7/a’ (swearing) do not apply.’”
